s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic scalp lesions with disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages
salient_findings: Nonhealing crusted scalp lesions for 3 years
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on biopsy
key_facts: 4-year-old boy
3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions
Previous treatments with topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics showed no improvement
Occasional otitis media
Negative family history for skin disease
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Normal routine blood examinations
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull on whole-body MRI
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on punch biopsy of scalp
Infiltrate stained positively for CD1A on immunohistochemical staining
Normal ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes
Normal serum electrophoresis

differentials: disseminated cryptococcosis due to cryptococcus laurentii

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: CD1A positivity and subepidermal infiltrate with kidney-shaped nuclei

shortlist.label: Disseminated histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Disseminated erythematous papules and osteolytic lesions

shortlist.label: Incontinentia pigmenti
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring skin lesions with atypical lymphocytes

shortlist.label: Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Nonhealing crusted scalp lesions and osteolytic lesions

raw.rationale: The presence of osteolytic lesions, subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei, and positive staining for CD1A on immunohistochemical staining are characteristic findings of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Disseminated histoplasmosis
rejected.why: No evidence of fungal infection or granulomatous reaction on biopsy

rejected.label: Incontinentia pigmenti
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic skin lesions and no family history of the disease

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: Absence of atypical lymphocytes and lack of response to treatments do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Histiocytosis
rejected.why: Too broad, Langerhans cell histiocytosis is a more specific diagnosis that fits the clinical and pathological findings
